title: Affidavit in support of an application for bail
ruleSource: Written from S.A Badmus' Criminal Litigation drafts (Lawdeck knowledge base). To be confirmed by the legal reviewer, including every statutory provision cited.

parts.why: Names the court, the judicial division and where it sits. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).
Names the court, the judicial division and where it sits. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.text:
CHARGE NO: {{chargeNumber}}
BETWEEN:
{{complainant}} .................... COMPLAINANT/RESPONDENT
AND
{{defendant}} .................... DEFENDANT/APPLICANT
parts.why: The charge number and the parties exactly as on the charge. Use 'Defendant', not 'Accused', and the defendant's full name (with any alias given). In Lagos the State is 'The State of Lagos'; in the FCT the Commissioner of Police or the Federal Republic of Nigeria, as on the charge. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.text: AFFIDAVIT IN SUPPORT OF THE APPLICATION FOR BAIL
parts.why: Names the document and what it supports. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.text: I, {{deponent}}, {{deponentDescription}}, of {{deponentAddress}}, do hereby make oath and state as follows:
parts.why: The deponent's name, description (adult, sex, religion, occupation, nationality) and address. Use the defendant as the deponent where the facts allow. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.instruction: Write the numbered paragraphs of an affidavit in support of bail, in the first person of the deponent, from the facts given: that the deponent is the defendant and knows the facts; the arrest and the offence alleged; the charge and any refusal of bail by a lower court (exhibiting the charge sheet and ruling as Exhibits A and B); the grounds for bail, such as ill health supported by a medical report as an exhibit, that the deponent will not jump bail, interfere with witnesses or commit an offence, and has reliable sureties. Facts only, no legal argument or conclusions. Start each paragraph with 'That'.
parts.why: The facts relied on, in numbered paragraphs: facts only, no argument, each exhibit identified. In the exam, the grounds for bail and the refusal by a lower court (with the ruling exhibited) carry the marks. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

parts.text:
That I swear to this affidavit in good faith, conscientiously believing its contents to be true and correct, and in accordance with the Oaths Act.

........................................
DEPONENT

Sworn to at the High Court Registry, {{sittingPlace}}
this ............ day of ............ 20.....

BEFORE ME

........................................
COMMISSIONER FOR OATHS
parts.why: The closing paragraph under the Oaths Act, the deponent's signature, the jurat (where and when it was sworn) and the Commissioner for Oaths. Source: Criminal Litigation drafting materials (Lawdeck knowledge base).

fields.label: Judicial division
fields.question: Which judicial division is the charge in? For example: Ikeja.

fields.label: Charge number
fields.question: The charge number, if known. Leave it empty to show a blank for it.

fields.label: Complainant
fields.question: Who is the complainant on the charge? For example: The State of Lagos.

fields.label: Defendant
fields.question: The defendant's full name, as on the charge.

fields.label: Deponent
fields.question: Who swears the affidavit? Usually the defendant.

fields.label: Deponent's description
fields.question: Describe the deponent: adult, sex, religion, occupation and nationality.
